newsitem.title: USA: Investment advisor admits stealing from clients.
newsitem.headline: Investment advisor admits stealing from clients.

text.p: An investment advisor has pleaded guilty to stealing more than $60 million from clients, mostly wealthy Filipinos, and defrauding them of millions of dollars in unearned fees, federal prosecutors said on Wednesday.

Teresa Fernandez, 49, of Tenafly, N.J., pleaded guilty to three counts of mail fraud in federal court late on Tuesday. She was president and owner of Wharton Investments Inc., which she operated from her home, prosecutors said.
She faces up to five years in prison on each count.

In a separate civil complaint filed on Tuesday, the Securities and Exchange Commission accused Fernandez of fraud for misappropriating $64 million in client funds by allegedly forging broker account statements and falsifying instructions to brokers.

Fernandez settled the SEC complaint without admitting or denying guilt by promising not to further violate federal securities laws. The SEC is still seeking an order for her to return illegal gains and to pay civil fines.

The criminal charges state that, starting in 1990, Fernandez opened securities trading accounts at Bear, Stearns & Co. on behalf of her clients. She had discretionary trading authority on the accounts but was not authorised to make withdrawals.
At the same time the accounts at Bear Stearns were opened, Fernandez secretly opened accounts at the Bank of New York in the same names as the Bear Stearns client accounts.

The complaint charges that she used forged letters of authorisation to get Bear Stearns to transfer more than $60 million from the accounts of her clients to the Bank of New York accounts she had established and controlled.

The clients entrusted more than $120 million to her between 1990 and 1995, with one unidentified Filipino investor giving her more than $50 million to invest through two of the three accounts, court papers said.
